title: Novel Drosophila cis -regulatory elements can be uncovered by footprinting transcription factor binding sites in ATAC-seq data
authors: Christian Mei; Jillian Ness; Katherine Nakai; Zeba Wunderlich
one_liner_zh: 该文利用ATAC-seq足迹分析预测果蝇转录因子结合位点并发现新顺式调控元件，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点预测，但主要基于序列足迹统计而非三维互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作的应用研究。
abstract: Developmental processes depend on carefully coordinated gene expression. Expression is modulated by the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to cis-regulatory elements (CREs), like enhancers and promoters. Many computational and experimental approaches have been developed to find CREs, particularly enhancers, in the genome, each with strengths and caveats. Given the increasing availability of ATAC-seq data and methods to find TF binding therein, we hypothesized that we could use TF footprinting tools to find clusters of TF binding events within accessible chromatin that may act as CREs. Using Drosophila anterior-posterior patterning network as a test bed, we used a digital genomic footprinting tool (DGT), TOBIAS, on previously published early embryo ATAC-seq data to characterize the TF footprint landscape of 16 TFs essential for embryonic patterning. Even in this system, with its extensive enhancer annotation, most footprinted TF binding sites lie outside of known enhancers, with intergenic and intronic regions hosting the highest TF footprint count, albeit at low density. To find potential novel enhancers, we identified high-density TF footprint clusters that are highly conserved and overlap with active enhancer histone mark signals. Five high confidence candidates were selected for reporter assay validation and all five were found to drive spatially patterned expression in the embryo. This study shows that even in a highly characterized system, the analysis of footprinted TF binding sites in ATAC-seq data can uncover new regulatory regions and suggests this approach may be helpful in using existing ATAC-seq data to find novel CREs. ARTICLE SUMMARY Given the increasing availability of ATAC-seq datasets, workflows to exploit the data to uncover new cis-regulatory elements (CREs), including enhancers, are valuable. Using early anterior-posterior patterning in the Drosophila embryo as a test case, we find that previously published transcription factor footprinting tools and ATAC-seq data can be analyzed to yield new candidate CREs. Experimental validation confirms the activity of selected candidate CREs, suggesting that existing data can be analyzed to find novel regulatory elements.
abstract_zh: 发育过程依赖于精细协调的基因表达。表达通过转录因子（TFs）与顺式调控元件（CREs），如增强子和启动子的结合来调节。许多计算和实验方法已被开发用于在基因组中寻找CREs，特别是增强子，每种方法各有优势和局限性。鉴于ATAC-seq数据的日益可得以及在其中寻找TF结合位点的方法，我们假设可以利用TF足迹分析工具在可及染色质内找到可能作为CREs的TF结合事件簇。以果蝇前后轴模式网络为测试平台，我们使用数字基因组足迹分析工具（DGT）TOBIAS，对先前发表的早期胚胎ATAC-seq数据进行分析，以表征对胚胎模式形成至关重要的16个TFs的TF足迹景观。即使在该系统中，尽管增强子注释广泛，大多数足迹化的TF结合位点仍位于已知增强子之外，其中基因间区和内含子区域承载最高的TF足迹计数，尽管密度较低。为发现潜在的新型增强子，我们鉴定了高密度TF足迹簇，这些簇高度保守且与活性增强子组蛋白标记信号重叠。五个高置信度候选被选用于报告基因检测验证，所有五个均被发现在胚胎中驱动空间模式化表达。本研究显示，即使在高度特征化的系统中，对ATAC-seq数据中足迹化TF结合位点的分析也能揭示新的调控区域，并表明该方法可能有助于利用现有ATAC-seq数据发现新型CREs。文章摘要 鉴于ATAC-seq数据集的日益可得，利用这些数据揭示新的顺式调控元件（CREs），包括增强子的工作流程具有重要价值。以果蝇胚胎早期前后轴模式为测试案例，我们发现先前发表的转录因子足迹分析工具和ATAC-seq数据可以被分析以产生新的候选CREs。实验验证确认了选定候选CREs的活性，表明现有数据可以被分析以发现新型调控元件。
